stories.title: Update: Jamia moves all classes online; registrar says union polls will follow draft constitution
stories.body: Jamia Millia Islamia moved all courses online with immediate effect and until further notice on Saturday 24 October, calling it a precautionary measure for student safety, India.com reported. The same day, ANI reported that Registrar Md. Mahtab Alam Rizvi met the hunger-striking students on the 13th day of a protest that began on Monday 12 October. He said elections will be announced once a draft students' union constitution is submitted by a committee that includes student representatives, and that disciplinary cases will be reviewed, with students found innocent reinstated. The students want the union, dissolved in 2006, restored, disciplinary action revoked and the Chief Proctor removed. Five students were reported still on strike.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: the registrar also alleged unauthorised entry onto campus by outside visitors, a police complaint, and 'Free Kashmir' graffiti; these are his statements and are unverified (a visiting MP, per ANI, denied slogans were raised). Reports differ on strike day count (12th vs 13th) and start date (12 Oct vs 13 Oct elsewhere). Confirm the online-class notice and current status with Jamia; no press release after 21 Oct on the strike was found.

CV Raman Marg Daily Brief, Sun 25 Oct

Jamia: all classes moved online from Sat 24 Oct until further notice (India.com). Registrar says union elections will be announced once the draft constitution is submitted; hunger strike (since 12 Oct) was on day 13, five students reported on strike (ANI).

No confirmed BSES, DJB, MCD, Delhi Police or Delhi Traffic Police items for our localities.
